A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bringing Your Portrait to 3D Presence. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction comparisons, quantitative ablations and qualitative tracking and animation results, including Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds head reenactment measurements in Table 4 and qualitative experiments in Figures 19–24.

M1.justification: The Dual-UV architecture, synthetic-data pipeline, training losses and proxy-mesh tracker remain unchanged. The added shell-mask sentence clarifies masking already represented in the existing formula; the GSM discussion explains the retained design rather than introducing a component.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds explicit cross-identity head reenactment evaluation on RenderMe360, extending the previously reported head evaluation. The original head, upper-body and full-body datasets and synthetic training sources are retained.

E2.justification: Table 4 and Figure 20 add GAGAvatar as a head reenactment comparator alongside LAM. V1 used GAGAvatar's tracking pipeline but did not evaluate its avatar outputs as a baseline. The original comparison sets remain intact.

E3.justification: The added cross-reenactment protocol uses 10 additional driving identities and evaluates CSIM, average expression distance and average pose distance. These metrics also supplement self-reenactment evaluation. The original training budget, train/validation split and benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds qualitative ablations for shell tokens, decoder depth, data scale and data type in Figure 22, targeted occlusion/hair failure examples in Figure 23, and additional viewpoint and pose examples. These supplement existing analyses; Table 2's quantitative ablation configurations and scores are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates; its additional driving identities are evaluation samples rather than repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their values, while Table 4 adds head reenactment results and Figures 19–24 add qualitative outcomes. Cross-reenactment favors Ours on AED/APD (0.2720/0.1299), but its CSIM is 0.6161 versus 0.6248 for LAM and 0.6536 for GAGAvatar. Table 4's LAM self-reenactment reconstruction scores match the earlier LAM† row, not a demonstrated improvement over the original unparsed LAM setting.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for UV projection, shell construction, losses, camera correction and tracking objectives are retained. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution claims retain the same scope: unified head/upper/full-body reconstruction, Dual-UV representation, synthetic-data training and robust tracking. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly explains heavy-occlusion and complex-hair failures through incomplete evidence and geometry/appearance ambiguity. It also suggests that residual tracking misalignment reduces ablation metric sensitivity. Existing limitations concerning proxy meshes, sparse viewpoints and synthetic-data artifacts remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents head sampling more explicitly as one clip per identity and clarifies shell masking. It removes the introduction's promise to release code upon acceptance, while retaining Appendix C.3's reference to released code; this changes access documentation without establishing actual availability. Numerical implementation settings, hardware and training time remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 expands citations to head-avatar work, including Portrait4D, Portrait4Dv2, Joker and UIKA. Appendix A.1 explicitly distinguishes Shell-UV feature projection from GSM's additional Gaussian layers. These are localized additions to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 merges the head/body and portrait related-work subsections under Human Modeling, makes localized wording and terminology corrections, and updates an author affiliation. Appendix D's ethics statement is replaced by More Experiments; most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The original 18 figure images and Tables 1–3 are retained. V2 adds Table 4 and Figures 19–24, with localized resizing, reflow and caption edits; the additions are concentrated in the appendix rather than constituting a document-wide redesign.

improvement.justification: The added head baseline, identity/motion metrics, qualitative ablations and explicit failure examples improve empirical scrutiny and make limitations easier to assess. The gain is limited: the principal experiments remain unchanged, Figure 20's identity-preservation wording does not acknowledge Table 4's CSIM disadvantage, and the explicit code-release promise is removed.
